/**
 * WriteSpeare — dashboard shell.
 *
 * This is the component `<Routes>` renders as the element of the
 * `/dashboard` route (see `renderer/App.tsx`). It is the
 * authenticated frame that every signed-in page lives inside: a
 * sidebar on the left, a main content area on the right, and an
 * `<Outlet />` in the content area where the currently-matched
 * child route (Topics, Topic Detail, Settings, Admin) renders.
 *
 * The component has exactly two responsibilities:
 *
 *   1. Auth gate — before any dashboard content mounts, verify
 *      that the user is authenticated. If the session is still
 *      being restored, render nothing (the alternative — a
 *      brief flash of the login page — would be wrong, and a
 *      brief flash of the dashboard — also wrong, because it
 *      would show stale or empty data). If the session has been
 *      restored and the user is not authenticated, redirect to
 *      `/login`. Only after a definitive answer is available
 *      does the dashboard tree mount.
 *
 *   2. Layout composition — render `<Sidebar />` on the left and
 *      a scrollable main region on the right. The sidebar's
 *      collapsed/expanded state is owned here and passed down as
 *      a controlled prop, so that `Sidebar` itself is stateless
 *      and easy to test in isolation.
 *
 * Why the auth gate lives here and not in each page:
 *
 *   The alternative would be for every authenticated page to
 *   check `useAuth()` on mount and redirect if the user is
 *   missing. That pattern duplicates the check across five or
 *   more files, and — more importantly — it duplicates the
 *   redirect. If two pages disagree about where an
 *   unauthenticated user should go (say, one sends them to
 *   `/login` and another to `/`), the app produces inconsistent
 *   behaviour depending on which route the user hit first.
 *
 *   Putting the gate in `Layout` means the invariant is enforced
 *   in exactly one place, and it is enforced BEFORE the child
 *   route renders. A page component never has to think about
 *   whether the user is signed in — by the time it renders, the
 *   answer is always "yes".
 *
 * The loading state:
 *
 *   When `isLoading` is `true`, the component returns `null`.
 *   That produces a blank frame for the brief window (usually a
 *   few dozen milliseconds) while the auth store reads the
 *   cached user from the encrypted store. The blank frame is
 *   preferable to either alternative:
 *
 *     - A loading spinner would flash on every cold start, even
 *       for users who are already signed in. The flash would be
 *       noticeable because it appears and disappears too fast to
 *       read, which reads as a glitch.
 *
 *     - Falling through to the login page would cause a redirect
 *       flash for users who are about to be authenticated. The
 *       address bar would show `/login` for a moment before
 *       being replaced by `/dashboard/topics`, and the user's
 *       back button would carry a history entry they did not
 *       create.
 *
 *   Returning `null` produces neither artifact. The cost is a
 *   briefly-empty window, which most users will not notice.
 *
 * Why the redirect uses `replace`:
 *
 *   `<Navigate to="/login" replace />` replaces the current
 *   history entry rather than pushing a new one. Without
 *   `replace`, an unauthenticated user who manually typed
 *   `/dashboard/topics` would press the back button from the
 *   login page and land back on `/dashboard/topics`, which
 *   would immediately redirect them to `/login` again — an
 *   inescapable loop. Replacing the entry closes that loop: the
 *   back button takes them to whatever page preceded their
 *   navigation into the dashboard, not into a redirect cycle.
 *
 * The scroll model:
 *
 *   The outer container is `flex h-full w-full overflow-hidden`
 *   — it fills its parent (the app root, which is set to `h-full`
 *   by the base styles in `tailwind.css`) and clips any overflow.
 *
 *   The sidebar is a fixed-width column that does not scroll —
 *   its internal content is designed to fit the viewport, and
 *   any rare overflow is handled by the sidebar's own
 *   `overflow-y-auto` on its nav element.
 *
 *   The main region is `flex-1 overflow-y-auto`, which makes it
 *   the only scrolling surface in the layout. A long page inside
 *   the `<Outlet />` scrolls the main region while the sidebar
 *   stays put — the standard behaviour for a persistent-nav app.
 *
 * Forward reference:
 *
 *   Like `Sidebar.tsx`, this file depends on `useAuth` from
 *   `apps/desktop/src/features/auth/hooks/useAuth.ts` — a file
 *   scheduled for Session 6. The import specifier therefore
 *   produces one `TS2307` until that file exists. This is the
 *   same forward-reference shape already logged by multiple
 *   files earlier in the session (`main/store.ts`,
 *   `main/preload.ts`, `renderer/App.tsx`, and the previous file
 *   `Sidebar.tsx`).
 *
 * Why there is no `LayoutProps` interface with fields:
 *
 *   The component takes no props today — the sidebar's collapsed
 *   state is internal to this file, and every other piece of the
 *   layout is derived from the router context or the auth store.
 *   The `LayoutProps` type is declared as an empty interface so
 *   that a future addition (for example, a `hideSidebar` prop
 *   for a full-screen view) has a named, exported home. An empty
 *   interface is a legal TypeScript construct and does not fail
 *   under any strict flag; it costs nothing and pre-declares the
 *   growth point.
 */

import { useState } from 'react';
import { Navigate, Outlet } from 'react-router-dom';

import { useAuth } from '../../auth/hooks/useAuth.js';
import Sidebar from './Sidebar.js';

// ============================================================
//  Public types
// ============================================================

/**
 * The props accepted by `Layout`. Currently empty — see the file
 * header for why the interface is declared anyway.
 */
// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-empty-object-type
export interface LayoutProps {
  // Reserved for future additions. See file header.
}

// ============================================================
//  Layout
// ============================================================

/**
 * The authenticated dashboard shell. See the file header for the
 * component's two responsibilities and the reasoning behind the
 * auth-gate and loading-state decisions.
 */
export const Layout = (_props: LayoutProps = {}) => {
  const { user, isLoading } = useAuth();

  /**
   * The sidebar's collapsed state. Owned here, passed to
   * `<Sidebar />` as a controlled prop. The initial value is
   * `false` — every fresh session starts with the sidebar
   * expanded, which is the recommended default for a user who is
   * about to navigate. If a future session wants to persist the
   * user's preference across restarts, the persistence call goes
   * in this file (the sole owner of the state), not in
   * `Sidebar.tsx`.
   */
  const [sidebarCollapsed, setSidebarCollapsed] = useState(false);

  /**
   * Flip the sidebar's collapsed state. Written as a functional
   * state update (`prev => !prev`) rather than a direct read of
   * `sidebarCollapsed` so that a rapid double-click produces two
   * toggles, not one — the direct form would compute both
   * updates from the same stale `sidebarCollapsed` value and
   * collapse into a single flip.
   */
  const toggleSidebar = (): void => {
    setSidebarCollapsed((prev) => !prev);
  };

  // ---- Auth gate: loading ----
  // The auth store has not yet determined whether a session
  // exists. Return null to avoid the two visual artifacts
  // described in the file header. See the file header for the
  // full reasoning.
  if (isLoading) {
    return null;
  }

  // ---- Auth gate: not authenticated ----
  // The auth store has resolved and there is no user. Redirect
  // to the login page with `replace` so the back button does not
  // loop. See the file header for the loop explanation.
  if (!user) {
    return <Navigate to="/login" replace />;
  }

  // ---- Authenticated ----
  // The user is signed in. Render the shell. Every child route
  // mounted inside `<Outlet />` can rely on `useAuth()` returning
  // a non-null `user`, because this component does not render its
  // children until the check above has passed.
  return (
    <div className="flex h-full w-full overflow-hidden bg-background">
      <Sidebar collapsed={sidebarCollapsed} onToggle={toggleSidebar} />

      {/*
        * The main content region. `flex-1` takes all remaining
        * horizontal space; `overflow-y-auto` makes this element
        * the app's only scrolling surface, so a long page inside
        * the Outlet scrolls here while the sidebar stays fixed.
        * `min-w-0` is required so that a flex child can shrink
        * below its content width when a descendant has
        * `whitespace-nowrap` or a wide table — without it, the
        * sidebar would be pushed off-screen by such content.
        */}
      <main className="min-w-0 flex-1 overflow-y-auto">
        <Outlet />
      </main>
    </div>
  );
};

// ============================================================
//  Default export
// ============================================================

/**
 * The `Layout` component as the default export, matching the
 * convention used by every other component file in the codebase.
 * `renderer/App.tsx` uses the default form
 * (`import Layout from '.../Layout.js'`), so this is the export
 * that keeps the route tree resolving.
 */
export default Layout;
</file>

<file path="apps/desktop/src/features/shared/components/Modal.tsx">
/**
 * WriteSpeare — reusable modal system.
 *
 * This module provides the app's modals — dialogs that block
 * interaction with the rest of the UI while the user reads the
 * message and acts on it. Two entry points compose the system:
 *
 *   `<Modal open={...} onClose={...}>` — the declarative
 *     component. Used by a component that wants to control a
 *     modal's visibility with its own state. This is the direct
 *     interpretation of the plan's description of this file.
 *
 *   `useModal()` — the imperative hook. Used by a component that
 *     wants to fire a modal — typically a confirmation, a
 *     warning, an informational notice — from an event handler
 *     or an async flow where threading a boolean state through
 *     the tree would be noise. The hook's `open(options)` method
 *     accepts the modal's content and configuration, and returns
 *     an id that can later be passed to `close(id)`.
 *
 * Both entry points share the internal `ModalShell` component —
 * the visual structure (backdrop, container, header, body,
 * footer) and the accessibility behaviours (focus trap, Escape
 * key, click-outside). Two entry points, one shell: the design
 * and the behaviours cannot drift between them because they are
 * the same code.
 *
 * What "handles Escape, overlay click, focus trap" means:
 *
 *   Escape — pressing the Escape key closes the modal, unless
 *     the caller has opted out via `closeOnEscape: false`. The
 *     listener runs in the capture phase and stops the event's
 *     propagation, so an inner component that also listens for
 *     Escape (a nested dropdown, for example) does not
 *     accidentally intercept the key.
 *
 *   Overlay click — clicking the backdrop (the dark area around
 *     the modal's content) closes the modal, unless the caller
 *     has opted out via `closeOnOverlay: false`. Clicks inside
 *     the modal's content area do NOT close — the content
 *     stops propagation, so a click on a form field or a button
 *     is not interpreted as a dismiss.
 *
 *   Focus trap — when the modal opens, focus moves into it.
 *     Pressing Tab cycles forward through the focusable
 *     elements inside the modal, wrapping from the last back to
 *     the first. Shift+Tab cycles backward, wrapping from the
 *     first to the last. The modal's container has `tabIndex
 *     ={-1}` so it can itself receive focus when the modal has
 *     no focusable children, in which case the trap is a no-op
 *     (there is nothing to cycle through) but focus is still
 *     kept inside the modal.
 *
 *   On close, focus is restored to whichever element had focus
 *   before the modal opened. That is the standard "focus
 *   restoration" behaviour — without it, keyboard users would
 *   find themselves at the top of the document after dismissing
 *   a modal, having to navigate back to wherever they were.
 *
 * Body scroll lock:
 *
 *   While any modal is open, the page behind it is prevented
 *   from scrolling. Without this, a user who scrolls the
 *   mouse-wheel while a modal is open would scroll the
 *   underlying content, which is disorienting when the modal
 *   covers most of the viewport. The lock is implemented with a
 *   module-level counter: the first modal to open sets
 *   `document.body.style.overflow = 'hidden'`, the last one to
 *   close restores it. The counter is what makes the lock
 *   correct when two modals stack — closing the top one does
 *   not unlock the body while the bottom one is still open.
 *
 * Variants — what each conveys:
 *
 *   info    — neutral information. Blue circle-i icon. Used
 *             for "here is what is about to happen" dialogs
 *             before a non-destructive action.
 *
 *   warning — a caution. Amber triangle icon. Used for "this
 *             will overwrite your existing work" dialogs that
 *             the user should read carefully but that are not
 *             irreversible.
 *
 *   danger  — a destructive action. Red circle-x icon. Used
 *             for delete confirmations and other irreversible
 *             operations.
 *
 *   success — a completed action worth acknowledging. Green
 *             check icon. Used sparingly — most completions
 *             are better handled by a toast than a modal, but
 *             a modal that reports the outcome of a long-
 *             running operation (an article export, a bulk
 *             delete) can be appropriate.
 *
 *   The variant affects the icon and its color at the top of
 *   the modal's header. It does not affect the modal's size,
 *   the buttons in the footer, or any other visual element.
 *   The caller chooses those independently, so a danger modal
 *   with a "Cancel" button whose color comes from the button's
 *   own styling is a natural composition.
 *
 * Sizes — what each is for:
 *
 *   sm   — confirmations. "Delete this topic?" A message and
 *          two buttons. 24rem wide.
 *   md   — the default. Short forms, informational dialogs,
 *          anything that fits in a few lines. 32rem wide.
 *   lg   — the standard for form-like dialogs. 42rem wide.
 *   xl   — the standard for dialogs with substantial content —
 *          a document preview, a settings pane. 56rem wide.
 *   full — a dialog that takes almost the whole viewport, for
 *          content that needs the room — a full-page document
 *          reader, a data-heavy report. 95vw by 95vh.
 */

import {
  createContext,
  useCallback,
  useContext,
  useEffect,
  useMemo,
  useRef,
  useState,
  type ReactNode,
} from 'react';
import { createPortal } from 'react-dom';
import { AnimatePresence, motion } from 'framer-motion';
import {
  AlertTriangle,
  CheckCircle,
  Info,
  X,
  XCircle,
  type LucideIcon,
} from 'lucide-react';

// ============================================================
//  Public types
// ============================================================

/**
 * The four variants a modal can take. See the file header for
 * the semantic meaning of each.
 */
export type ModalVariant = 'info' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'success';

/**
 * The five sizes a modal can take. See the file header for the
 * recommended use of each.
 */
export type ModalSize = 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' | 'full';

/**
 * The props accepted by the `Modal` component — the declarative
 * entry point. Every field except `open`, `onClose`, and
 * `children` is optional.
 */
export interface ModalProps {
  /** Whether the modal is currently visible. */
  open: boolean;

  /** Called when the modal should close, by any of the three
   *  paths (Escape, overlay click, or a caller-triggered
   *  dismissal). The caller is responsible for flipping its own
   *  `open` state in response. */
  onClose: () => void;

  /** Visual variant. Defaults to `'info'`. */
  variant?: ModalVariant;

  /** Size class. Defaults to `'md'`. */
  size?: ModalSize;

  /** Optional title shown at the top of the modal's header. */
  title?: string;

  /** Whether clicking the backdrop closes the modal. Defaults
   *  to `true`. */
  closeOnOverlay?: boolean;

  /** Whether pressing Escape closes the modal. Defaults to
   *  `true`. */
  closeOnEscape?: boolean;

  /** Whether to render the X button in the top-right corner of
   *  the header. Defaults to `true`. */
  showCloseButton?: boolean;

  /** Extra Tailwind classes appended to the modal's content
   *  container. Useful for a caller that needs to widen the
   *  container past the size preset, or to add a per-instance
   *  background. */
  className?: string;

  /** Optional footer content — typically the modal's action
   *  buttons. Rendered below the body, separated by a border
   *  and given the horizontal alignment the plan's mockups
   *  specify (right-aligned on desktop). */
  footer?: ReactNode;

  /** The modal's body. */
  children: ReactNode;
}

/**
 * The options accepted by `useModal().open(...)`. Structurally
 * the same set of fields as `ModalProps` minus `open` (always
 * true for an imperatively-opened modal) and minus `children`
 * (renamed to `content` so the shape reads naturally as an
 * options object rather than as JSX attributes).
 */
export interface ModalOptions {
  title?: string;
  variant?: ModalVariant;
  size?: ModalSize;
  content: ReactNode;
  footer?: ReactNode;
  closeOnOverlay?: boolean;
  closeOnEscape?: boolean;
  showCloseButton?: boolean;
  className?: string;

  /** Called when the modal is dismissed, by any of the three
   *  paths. This is a notification, not a veto — by the time it
   *  fires, the modal is already closing. */
  onClose?: () => void;
}

/**
 * The shape of the object returned by `useModal()`.
 */
export interface ModalAPI {
  /**
   * Open a modal imperatively. Returns an id that can be passed
   * to `close(id)` to dismiss that specific modal — useful when
   * a modal is opened from an async flow and the flow resolves
   * before the user acts, at which point the modal is stale.
   */
  open: (options: ModalOptions) => string;

  /**
   * Close a specific modal by id, or the topmost modal when no
   * id is given. A no-op if no modal is currently open, or if
   * the id does not match a visible modal.
   */
  close: (id?: string) => void;

  /** Close every visible modal at once. */
  closeAll: () => void;
}

// ============================================================
//  Internal types
// ============================================================

/**
 * A modal record held by the provider's state. `closing` is set
 * to `true` when the modal is being dismissed — the record stays
 * in the state array during the exit animation and is removed
 * once the animation completes.
 */
interface ModalRecord {
  id: string;
  options: ModalOptions;
  closing: boolean;
}

// ============================================================
//  Constants
// ============================================================

/**
 * The selector that matches any element that can receive focus.
 * Used by the focus trap to enumerate the candidates inside the
 * modal's content container.
 *
 * The `:not([disabled])` and `:not([tabindex="-1"])` guards
 * exclude elements that are technically focusable per the DOM
 * but that the user cannot reach with the keyboard. A
 * `<button disabled>` is not tabbable, and neither is an
 * element with an explicit `tabindex="-1"` (which is how the
 * modal's own container is made programmatically focusable
 * without becoming a tab stop).
 */
const FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR =
  'a[href], button:not([disabled]), input:not([disabled]), ' +
  'textarea:not([disabled]), select:not([disabled]), ' +
  '[tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])';

/**
 * The duration, in milliseconds, of the modal's enter and exit
 * animations. Must match the `transition.duration` values passed
 * to the framer-motion elements below. Named as a constant so
 * the two places that reference it — the animation and the
 * imperative provider's post-animation cleanup timeout — stay in
 * sync.
 */
const ANIMATION_DURATION_MS = 200;

/**
 * The size classes, keyed by `ModalSize`. Declared as a
 * `Record<ModalSize, string>` so that the compiler enforces
 * exhaustiveness: adding a sixth size to the union without
 * adding an entry here is a compile error.
 */
const SIZE_CLASSES: Record<ModalSize, string> = {
  sm: 'w-full max-w-sm',
  md: 'w-full max-w-lg',
  lg: 'w-full max-w-2xl',
  xl: 'w-full max-w-4xl',
  full: 'w-[95vw] h-[95vh]',
};

/**
 * The variant-specific icon and icon color. Same exhaustiveness
 * guarantee as `SIZE_CLASSES`. The color is deliberately the
 * icon's only variant-driven styling; a modal's overall container
 * background is neutral, so the same layout reads as "danger" or
 * "info" purely from the icon at the top of the header.
 */
const VARIANT_ICONS: Record<
  ModalVariant,
  { icon: LucideIcon; className: string }
> = {
  info: {
    icon: Info,
    className: 'text-sky-600 dark:text-sky-400',
  },
  warning: {
    icon: AlertTriangle,
    className: 'text-amber-600 dark:text-amber-400',
  },
  danger: {
    icon: XCircle,
    className: 'text-red-600 dark:text-red-400',
  },
  success: {
    icon: CheckCircle,
    className: 'text-emerald-600 dark:text-emerald-400',
  },
};

// ============================================================
//  Body scroll lock
// ============================================================
//
//  Module-level counter. See the file header for why a counter
//  is required rather than a simple boolean.

let scrollLockCount = 0;

/**
 * Acquire the body scroll lock. The first acquisition sets
 * `overflow: hidden` on the body; subsequent acquisitions are
 * no-ops that only increment the counter.
 */
const acquireScrollLock = (): void => {
  scrollLockCount += 1;
  if (scrollLockCount === 1) {
    document.body.style.overflow = 'hidden';
  }
};

/**
 * Release the body scroll lock. The last release restores the
 * body's default overflow; earlier releases are no-ops that only
 * decrement the counter. The `Math.max(0, ...)` guard prevents
 * the counter from going negative if release is called more
 * times than acquire (which would be a bug in this module, not
 * in a caller, but the guard keeps the failure mode harmless).
 */
const releaseScrollLock = (): void => {
  scrollLockCount = Math.max(0, scrollLockCount - 1);
  if (scrollLockCount === 0) {
    document.body.style.overflow = '';
  }
};

// ============================================================
//  ModalShell — shared visual structure and behaviours
// ============================================================
//
//  Both `Modal` (declarative) and `ModalProvider` (imperative)
//  render a `ModalShell`. The shell owns the backdrop, the
//  content container, the header, the body, the footer, and the
//  three accessibility behaviours (Escape, focus trap, focus
//  restoration). Nothing about the shell is animated — the
//  animation is applied by whichever parent renders it (the
//  declarative `Modal` or the provider's item).

interface ModalShellProps {
  variant: ModalVariant;
  size: ModalSize;
  title: string | undefined;
  closeOnOverlay: boolean;
  closeOnEscape: boolean;
  showCloseButton: boolean;
  className: string | undefined;
  footer: ReactNode;
  onClose: () => void;
  children: ReactNode;
}

/**
 * The internal modal structure. Not exported — no consumer
 * outside this module should render it directly.
 *
 * The shell is deliberately unaware of its own visibility state;
 * its parent decides when to mount and unmount it. This is what
 * lets the two parent components (declarative Modal, imperative
 * provider) share the shell while owning their own animation and
 * lifecycle logic.
 */
const ModalShell = ({
  variant,
  size,
  title,
  closeOnOverlay,
  closeOnEscape,
  showCloseButton,
  className,
  footer,
  onClose,
  children,
}: ModalShellProps) => {
  const contentRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);

  const { icon: Icon, className: iconClass } = VARIANT_ICONS[variant];
  const sizeClass = SIZE_CLASSES[size];

  // ---- Body scroll lock ----
  // Runs once per mounted shell. See the file header for why
  // the lock uses a counter rather than a boolean.
  useEffect(() => {
    acquireScrollLock();
    return () => {
      releaseScrollLock();
    };
  }, []);

  // ---- Focus management ----
  // On mount: save the currently-focused element, focus the
  // modal's content container (which is programmatically
  // focusable via tabIndex={-1}), and restore the previous focus
  // on unmount. The restoration runs in the cleanup so it fires
  // regardless of which path caused the unmount.
  //
  // The saved element is stored in a ref rather than state
  // because nothing about its identity needs to trigger a
  // re-render.
  const previouslyFocusedRef = useRef<HTMLElement | null>(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    const previouslyFocused = document.activeElement;
    previouslyFocusedRef.current =
      previouslyFocused instanceof HTMLElement ? previouslyFocused : null;

    // Focus the modal container. If the modal contains a
    // focusable element, `contentRef.current.focus()` moves
    // focus to the container itself; the browser's default
    // behavior on subsequent Tab presses then proceeds into
    // the first focusable descendant. Focusing the container
    // first (rather than the first focusable descendant
    // directly) is the standard behaviour — it ensures that
    // Escape works immediately on open, without the user having
    // to Tab first.
    contentRef.current?.focus();

    return () => {
      previouslyFocusedRef.current?.focus();
    };
  }, []);

  // ---- Keyboard handling ----
  // One listener covers Escape and Tab (for the focus trap).
  // Attached in the capture phase so it runs before React's
  // synthetic event system; the stopPropagation on Escape
  // prevents an inner component's own Escape handler from also
  // firing.
  useEffect(() => {
    const handleKeyDown = (event: KeyboardEvent): void => {
      // ---- Escape ----
      if (event.key === 'Escape' && closeOnEscape) {
        event.stopPropagation();
        onClose();
        return;
      }

      // ---- Tab (focus trap) ----
      if (event.key !== 'Tab') {
        return;
      }

      const container = contentRef.current;
      if (!container) {
        return;
      }

      const focusables =
        container.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR);

      // No focusable elements inside the modal. The container
      // itself is focusable (tabIndex={-1}), so we prevent Tab
      // from leaving it by keeping focus where it is.
      if (focusables.length === 0) {
        event.preventDefault();
        container.focus();
        return;
      }

      const first = focusables[0];
      const last = focusables[focusables.length - 1];
      if (!first || !last) {
        return;
      }

      const active = document.activeElement;

      if (event.shiftKey) {
        // Shift+Tab: if focus is on the first focusable (or
        // outside the modal), wrap to the last.
        if (active === first || !container.contains(active)) {
          event.preventDefault();
          last.focus();
        }
      } else {
        // Tab: if focus is on the last focusable (or outside
        // the modal), wrap to the first.
        if (active === last || !container.contains(active)) {
          event.preventDefault();
          first.focus();
        }
      }
    };

    document.addEventListener('keydown', handleKeyDown, true);
    return () => {
      document.removeEventListener('keydown', handleKeyDown, true);
    };
  }, [closeOnEscape, onClose]);

  // ---- Overlay click ----
  // The overlay click is distinguished from a click inside the
  // modal by comparing the event target to the current target.
  // A click on the backdrop's own surface (not on a descendant)
  // has `target === currentTarget`; a click on any child of the
  // modal content does not.
  const handleBackdropClick = (
    event: React.MouseEvent<HTMLDivElement>
  ): void => {
    if (!closeOnOverlay) {
      return;
    }
    if (event.target !== event.currentTarget) {
      return;
    }
    onClose();
  };

  return (
    <div
      onClick={handleBackdropClick}
      className={
        'fixed inset-0 z-40 flex items-center justify-center ' +
        'bg-black/50 p-4 backdrop-blur-sm'
      }
    >
      <div
        ref={contentRef}
        tabIndex={-1}
        role="dialog"
        aria-modal="true"
        aria-labelledby={title !== undefined ? 'modal-title' : undefined}
        className={
          'relative flex max-h-[90vh] flex-col overflow-hidden ' +
          'rounded-2xl bg-background shadow-medium outline-none ' +
          `${sizeClass} ` +
          (className ?? '')
        }
      >
        {/* ---- Header ---- */}
        {(title !== undefined || showCloseButton) && (
          <div className="flex items-start gap-3 border-b border-neutral-200 px-6 py-4 dark:border-neutral-800">
            <Icon size={22} className={`mt-0.5 shrink-0 ${iconClass}`} />

            {title !== undefined && (
              <h2
                id="modal-title"
                className="min-w-0 flex-1 text-base font-semibold leading-snug text-text dark:text-neutral-100"
              >
                {title}
              </h2>
            )}

            {title === undefined && <div className="flex-1" />}

            {showCloseButton && (
              <button
                type="button"
                onClick={onClose}
                aria-label="Close dialog"
                className={
                  'shrink-0 rounded-md p-1 text-neutral-500 ' +
                  'transition-colors hover:bg-neutral-100 hover:text-neutral-800 ' +
                  'dark:text-neutral-400 dark:hover:bg-neutral-800 dark:hover:text-neutral-100 ' +
                  'focus-visible:outline-none'
                }
              >
                <X size={18} />
              </button>
            )}
          </div>
        )}

        {/* ---- Body ---- */}
        <div className="min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-y-auto px-6 py-5 text-sm leading-relaxed text-text dark:text-neutral-100">
          {children}
        </div>

        {/* ---- Footer ---- */}
        {footer !== undefined && (
          <div className="flex items-center justify-end gap-2 border-t border-neutral-200 px-6 py-4 dark:border-neutral-800">
            {footer}
          </div>
        )}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
};

// ============================================================
//  Modal — declarative component
// ============================================================

/**
 * The declarative modal component. Renders a `ModalShell` inside
 * a `motion.div` wrapped by `AnimatePresence`, so that opening
 * and closing the modal plays an entrance and exit animation.
 *
 * The `open` prop controls visibility. When it flips from `true`
 * to `false`, `AnimatePresence` keeps the underlying content
 * mounted until the exit animation completes, then unmounts it.
 * The caller's `onClose` fires when the user dismisses the
 * modal (via Escape, backdrop click, or the close button) — the
 * caller is expected to flip its own `open` state in response,
 * which is what triggers the exit animation.
 *
 * When `open` is `false` on the first render, nothing is
 * rendered — no backdrop, no portal, no listeners. That is what
 * keeps a component that conditionally shows a modal from paying
 * any cost for the modal when it is not shown.
 */
export const Modal = ({
  open,
  onClose,
  variant = 'info',
  size = 'md',
  title,
  closeOnOverlay = true,
  closeOnEscape = true,
  showCloseButton = true,
  className,
  footer,
  children,
}: ModalProps) => {
  return createPortal(
    <AnimatePresence>
      {open && (
        <motion.div
          key="modal-backdrop"
          initial={{ opacity: 0 }}
          animate={{ opacity: 1 }}
          exit={{ opacity: 0 }}
          transition={{ duration: ANIMATION_DURATION_MS / 1000 }}
        >
          <ModalShell
            variant={variant}
            size={size}
            title={title}
            closeOnOverlay={closeOnOverlay}
            closeOnEscape={closeOnEscape}
            showCloseButton={showCloseButton}
            className={className}
            footer={footer}
            onClose={onClose}
          >
            {children}
          </ModalShell>
        </motion.div>
      )}
    </AnimatePresence>,
    document.body
  );
};

// ============================================================
//  Context
// ============================================================

const ModalContext = createContext<ModalAPI | null>(null);

// ============================================================
//  useModal hook
// ============================================================

/**
 * Return the imperative modal API from the enclosing
 * `ModalProvider`.
 *
 * Throws when called outside a provider — the same contract as
 * `useToast`. A component that expects to open modals but is
 * rendered outside the provider has a programming error that
 * would otherwise manifest as silently no-op calls.
 */
export const useModal = (): ModalAPI => {
  const ctx = useContext(ModalContext);
  if (!ctx) {
    throw new Error(
      'useModal() was called outside a <ModalProvider>. ' +
        'Make sure the component is rendered inside the app root.'
    );
  }
  return ctx;
};

// ============================================================
//  Provider
// ============================================================

/**
 * The context provider that owns the imperative modal stack and
 * renders the currently-open modals as portals.
 *
 * Mounted once, at the root of the renderer's component tree.
 * Everything below it can call `useModal().open({...})` to open
 * a modal imperatively.
 *
 * The provider keeps its modals in an array so that a second
 * modal can be opened on top of the first — a common pattern
 * for a confirmation dialog that appears over a form dialog.
 * Escape and overlay-click are handled by the topmost modal
 * only, because the `ModalShell` inside the topmost modal is
 * the last to attach its capture-phase listener.
 *
 * Exit animation timing:
 *
 *   When a modal is closed, the record's `closing` flag is set
 *   to `true` and the record is removed from the state array
 *   only after `ANIMATION_DURATION_MS + 50` milliseconds. The
 *   extra fifty milliseconds is a safety margin — it ensures
 *   the record is not removed before the animation has finished
 *   rendering, which would cause a visible flicker.
 */
export const ModalProvider = ({
  children,
}: {
  children: ReactNode;
}) => {
  const [records, setRecords] = useState<ModalRecord[]>([]);

  // A ref that always mirrors the latest records array. The
  // `close` callback below reads from this ref rather than from
  // the closure-captured state so that its identity stays stable
  // across renders — a consumer that lists `modal.close` in a
  // `useEffect` dependency array will not see it change on every
  // provider render.
  const recordsRef = useRef<ModalRecord[]>(records);
  recordsRef.current = records;

  /**
   * Generate a unique id for a new modal record. Same shape as
   * the id generator in `Toast.tsx`: a timestamp plus a random
   * suffix.
   */
  const generateId = (): string =>
    `${Date.now()}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 9)}`;

  /**
   * Mark a modal as closing and schedule its removal from the
   * state array after the exit animation completes. Called by
   * `close` (for a user-initiated close) and directly by the
   * `onClose` path when a modal dismisses itself.
   */
  const dismiss = useCallback((id: string): void => {
    setRecords((prev) =>
      prev.map((r) => (r.id === id ? { ...r, closing: true } : r))
    );
    setTimeout(() => {
      setRecords((prev) => prev.filter((r) => r.id !== id));
    }, ANIMATION_DURATION_MS + 50);
  }, []);

  /**
   * Open a modal and return its id.
   */
  const open = useCallback((options: ModalOptions): string => {
    const id = generateId();
    setRecords((prev) => [...prev, { id, options, closing: false }]);
    return id;
  }, []);

  /**
   * Close the modal with the given id, or the topmost modal when
   * no id is supplied. Invokes the caller's `onClose` before
   * starting the exit animation, so the caller's cleanup logic
   * (if any) runs before the modal starts to fade.
   */
  const close = useCallback(
    (id?: string): void => {
      const current = recordsRef.current;
      const target =
        id !== undefined
          ? current.find((r) => r.id === id)
          : current[current.length - 1];

      if (!target || target.closing) {
        return;
      }

      target.options.onClose?.();
      dismiss(target.id);
    },
    [dismiss]
  );

  /**
   * Close every visible modal. Unlike `close`, which respects
   * the caller's `onClose` and plays each modal's exit animation
   * separately, `closeAll` removes every record immediately —
   * the effect is an abrupt dismissal, which is the correct
   * behaviour when the app is logging out or resetting its
   * state.
   */
  const closeAll = useCallback((): void => {
    for (const record of recordsRef.current) {
      record.options.onClose?.();
    }
    setRecords([]);
  }, []);

  const api = useMemo<ModalAPI>(
    () => ({ open, close, closeAll }),
    [open, close, closeAll]
  );

  return (
    <ModalContext.Provider value={api}>
      {children}

      {records.map((record) => (
        <Modal
          key={record.id}
          open={!record.closing}
          onClose={() => close(record.id)}
          {...(record.options.title !== undefined
            ? { title: record.options.title }
            : {})}
          {...(record.options.variant !== undefined
            ? { variant: record.options.variant }
            : {})}
          {...(record.options.size !== undefined
            ? { size: record.options.size }
            : {})}
          {...(record.options.footer !== undefined
            ? { footer: record.options.footer }
            : {})}
          {...(record.options.closeOnOverlay !== undefined
            ? { closeOnOverlay: record.options.closeOnOverlay }
            : {})}
          {...(record.options.closeOnEscape !== undefined
            ? { closeOnEscape: record.options.closeOnEscape }
            : {})}
          {...(record.options.showCloseButton !== undefined
            ? { showCloseButton: record.options.showCloseButton }
            : {})}
          {...(record.options.className !== undefined
            ? { className: record.options.className }
            : {})}
        >
          {record.options.content}
        </Modal>
      ))}
    </ModalContext.Provider>
  );
};

// ============================================================
//  Default export
// ============================================================

/**
 * The `Modal` component as the default export, matching the
 * convention used by every other component file in the
 * codebase. Consumers that prefer the named form use
 * `import { Modal } from ...`; consumers that prefer the
 * default form use `import Modal from ...`. Both resolve to
 * the same component.
 */
export default Modal;
</file>

<file path="apps/desktop/src/features/shared/components/Sidebar.tsx">
/**
 * WriteSpeare — main navigation sidebar.
 *
 * This module provides the app's persistent left-hand sidebar,
 * the column that appears alongside every authenticated page (see
 * `Layout.tsx`, which mounts this component). It has four jobs:
 *
 *   1. Show the WriteSpeare brand at the top.
 *   2. Render the primary navigation links — Topics, Settings,
 *      and Admin (the last only for admin users).
 *   3. Show the currently authenticated user's email address.
 *   4. Offer a logout action.
 *
 * The component also exposes a collapse/expand toggle that lives
 * in its header. The state itself is NOT owned here — the parent
 * (`Layout.tsx`) owns it and passes it in via props, and the
 * toggle button calls back to the parent through `onToggle`.
 * That structure matches the plan's description of Layout
 * ("Sidebar toggle") and keeps the Sidebar a controlled
 * component whose only concern is rendering.
 *
 * Collapsed vs. expanded:
 *
 *   Expanded (default, ~15rem wide) — full navigation with
 *     labels, brand name, email, and a text-labeled logout
 *     button. This is the state for a user who is actively
 *     navigating.
 *
 *   Collapsed (~4rem wide) — icon-only navigation with a tooltip
 *     on hover for each icon, brand reduced to the logomark, no
 *     email, and an icon-only logout button. This is the state
 *     for a user who wants the sidebar out of the way while
 *     keeping the navigation reachable.
 *
 *   The width transition is animated over 200 ms so collapsing
 *   and expanding feel smooth rather than instant. The duration
 *   matches the animation durations used elsewhere in the app
 *   (`Toast.tsx`, `Modal.tsx`) so the whole UI has a consistent
 *   sense of pacing.
 *
 * Active-link highlighting:
 *
 *   Navigation uses `NavLink` from react-router-dom rather than
 *   `Link`. `NavLink` gives every consumer a boolean `isActive`
 *   through a render-prop callback, which the item uses to switch
 *   between the active style (brand-filled) and the inactive
 *   style (neutral hover). `NavLink` also sets
 *   `aria-current="page"` automatically on the active item, which
 *   is what assistive technology uses to announce "you are here".
 *
 *   The Topics link deliberately has NO `end` prop — the route
 *   `/dashboard/topics/:id` (a topic's detail page) is a
 *   descendant of `/dashboard/topics`, and the Topics link should
 *   stay highlighted while the user is on a detail page. The
 *   Settings and Admin links have no subroutes in the plan's
 *   route tree, so their default matching behaviour is correct.
 *
 * Forward reference:
 *
 *   The authenticated user comes from `useAuth()`, which is
 *   declared in `apps/desktop/src/features/auth/hooks/useAuth.ts`
 *   — a file scheduled for Session 6. Until that file exists,
 *   this module's import specifier `../../auth/hooks/useAuth.js`
 *   does not resolve and produces one `TS2307` error. That is
 *   expected and is the same shape as the forward references
 *   already logged by `renderer/App.tsx` (which waits on several
 *   feature pages) and by `main/preload.ts` (whose types file
 *   landed earlier in this session).
 *
 *   The plan does not declare a re-export shim for `useAuth` in
 *   the shared hooks folder, so this file imports the hook from
 *   its canonical location inside the auth feature. That import
 *   path is the same one the `Login` page and every future
 *   authenticated page will use.
 */

import {
  ChevronLeft,
  ChevronRight,
  Feather,
  FileText,
  LogOut,
  Settings as SettingsIcon,
  ShieldCheck,
  type LucideIcon,
} from 'lucide-react';
import { NavLink, type NavLinkRenderProps } from 'react-router-dom';

import { useAuth } from '../../auth/hooks/useAuth.js';
import { APP_NAME } from '../constants/index.js';

// ============================================================
//  Public types
// ============================================================

/**
 * The props accepted by the `Sidebar` component.
 *
 * The component is a controlled shell — it renders based on the
 * `collapsed` prop and notifies the parent when the toggle button
 * is clicked. The parent owns the state; the child never mutates
 * it directly.
 */
export interface SidebarProps {
  /** Whether the sidebar is currently in its narrow, icon-only
   *  form. The parent toggles this value in response to
   *  `onToggle`. */
  collapsed: boolean;

  /** Called when the user clicks the collapse/expand button.
   *  The parent is responsible for flipping its own state. */
  onToggle: () => void;
}

// ============================================================
//  NavItem — internal helper
// ============================================================

/**
 * Props for the internal `NavItem` helper. Not exported — the
 * helper is an implementation detail of this module.
 */
interface NavItemProps {
  /** The route the item navigates to. Matches a `path` in the
   *  app's route tree (see `renderer/App.tsx`). */
  to: string;

  /** The lucide icon rendered at the start of the item. */
  icon: LucideIcon;

  /** The item's label. Rendered as text when expanded and used
   *  as the tooltip (`title`) when collapsed. */
  label: string;

  /** Whether the sidebar is currently collapsed. Controls the
   *  item's spacing and whether the label is shown. */
  collapsed: boolean;
}

/**
 * Render a single navigation link. Used by `Sidebar` for each of
 * its three items. The `NavLink` render-prop form is what lets
 * the item switch styles based on the router's own active-route
 * determination, which is more reliable than re-deriving the
 * active state from `useLocation()` in the parent — it correctly
 * handles edge cases like nested routes and trailing slashes.
 */
const NavItem = ({ to, icon: Icon, label, collapsed }: NavItemProps) => {
  const className = ({ isActive }: NavLinkRenderProps): string => {
    const base =
      'flex items-center rounded-lg text-sm font-medium ' +
      'transition-colors focus-visible:outline-none';

    const spacing = collapsed
      ? 'justify-center p-2'
      : 'gap-3 px-3 py-2';

    const state = isActive
      ? 'bg-primary text-white'
      : 'text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 ' +
        'dark:text-neutral-300 dark:hover:bg-neutral-800';

    return `${base} ${spacing} ${state}`;
  };

  return (
    <NavLink to={to} className={className} title={collapsed ? label : undefined}>
      <Icon size={18} className="shrink-0" aria-hidden="true" />
      {!collapsed && <span className="truncate">{label}</span>}
    </NavLink>
  );
};

// ============================================================
//  Sidebar
// ============================================================

/**
 * The main navigation sidebar. See the file header for the
 * component's responsibilities, the collapsed/expanded state
 * contract, and the reasoning behind the design choices.
 */
export const Sidebar = ({ collapsed, onToggle }: SidebarProps) => {
  const { user, logout } = useAuth();

  /**
   * Whether the current user is an administrator. The Admin link
   * is rendered only when this is `true`. The role check itself
   * is a string comparison — `useAuth` returns the user object
   * as the backend serialized it, and the backend's `UserRole`
   * enum serializes to the string `'admin'`.
   */
  const isAdmin = user?.role === 'admin';

  /**
   * Log the user out. The actual state transitions — clearing
   * the token, clearing the cached user, notifying the main
   * process — are handled by `useAuth`'s `logout` function. This
   * handler exists only to give the click a place to attach and
   * to keep the component free of `void`-discarded floating
   * promises.
   *
   * The redirect back to `/login` is NOT performed here. It is
   * performed by `Layout.tsx`'s auth check, which runs whenever
   * the store's user becomes null — the same code path that
   * handles a session expiring during use. Keeping the redirect
   * in one place (Layout) rather than two (Layout and Sidebar)
   * is what prevents the two from disagreeing about when to
   * redirect.
   */
  const handleLogout = (): void => {
    void logout();
  };

  return (
    <aside
      className={
        'flex h-full flex-col border-r border-neutral-200 ' +
        'bg-background transition-[width] duration-200 ' +
        'dark:border-neutral-800 ' +
        (collapsed ? 'w-16' : 'w-60')
      }
    >
      {/* ---- Header ---- */}
      {/* The brand and the collapse/expand toggle. When expanded,
          the brand takes the horizontal space (flex-1) and pushes
          the toggle to the right edge; when collapsed, the toggle
          is centered. */}
      <div
        className={
          'flex h-14 shrink-0 items-center gap-2 px-3 ' +
          'border-b border-neutral-200 dark:border-neutral-800 ' +
          (collapsed ? 'justify-center' : '')
        }
      >
        {!collapsed && (
          <div className="flex flex-1 items-center gap-2 overflow-hidden">
            <Feather
              size={20}
              className="shrink-0 text-primary"
              aria-hidden="true"
            />
            <span className="truncate font-semibold text-text dark:text-neutral-100">
              {APP_NAME}
            </span>
          </div>
        )}

        <button
          type="button"
          onClick={onToggle}
          aria-label={collapsed ? 'Expand sidebar' : 'Collapse sidebar'}
          className={
            'shrink-0 rounded-md p-1 text-neutral-500 transition-colors ' +
            'hover:bg-neutral-100 hover:text-neutral-800 ' +
            'dark:text-neutral-400 dark:hover:bg-neutral-800 dark:hover:text-neutral-100 ' +
            'focus-visible:outline-none'
          }
        >
          {collapsed ? (
            <ChevronRight size={18} aria-hidden="true" />
          ) : (
            <ChevronLeft size={18} aria-hidden="true" />
          )}
        </button>
      </div>

      {/* ---- Navigation ---- */}
      {/* `flex-1` pushes the footer to the bottom; `overflow-y-auto`
          handles the case of an unusually large number of nav items
          (today there are at most three) without pushing the footer
          off-screen. */}
      <nav
        aria-label="Main navigation"
        className="flex-1 space-y-1 overflow-y-auto p-2"
      >
        <NavItem
          to="/dashboard/topics"
          icon={FileText}
          label="Topics"
          collapsed={collapsed}
        />

        <NavItem
          to="/dashboard/settings"
          icon={SettingsIcon}
          label="Settings"
          collapsed={collapsed}
        />

        {isAdmin && (
          <NavItem
            to="/dashboard/admin"
            icon={ShieldCheck}
            label="Admin"
            collapsed={collapsed}
          />
        )}
      </nav>

      {/* ---- Footer: user + logout ---- */}
      <div
        className={
          'shrink-0 border-t border-neutral-200 p-3 ' +
          'dark:border-neutral-800'
        }
      >
        {!collapsed && user && (
          <div
            className="mb-2 truncate px-1 text-xs text-neutral-500 dark:text-neutral-400"
            title={user.email}
          >
            {user.email}
          </div>
        )}

        {user && (
          <button
            type="button"
            onClick={handleLogout}
            title={collapsed ? 'Log out' : undefined}
            className={
              'flex w-full items-center rounded-lg text-sm font-medium ' +
              'text-neutral-700 transition-colors ' +
              'hover:bg-neutral-100 hover:text-neutral-900 ' +
              'dark:text-neutral-300 dark:hover:bg-neutral-800 dark:hover:text-neutral-100 ' +
              'focus-visible:outline-none ' +
              (collapsed
                ? 'justify-center p-2'
                : 'gap-3 px-3 py-2')
            }
          >
            <LogOut size={18} className="shrink-0" aria-hidden="true" />
            {!collapsed && <span className="truncate">Log out</span>}
          </button>
        )}
      </div>
    </aside>
  );
};
